name: Documentary & Field-Observation Video Briefs
body: # FLUX 3 documentary and nature prompts Six synthetic editorial concepts. Label generated scenes as reconstructions or illustrations; they are not recorded evidence of people, places or animal behavior. ## D01 — Before the first ferry **Use:** human-interest concept film **Mode:** text to video · **Format:** 16:9, 18 seconds **Adjust:** fictional harbor details without adding location claims. ```text An older ferry-terminal cleaner in a faded orange work jacket is finishing a bench before sunrise. One early passenger waits several steps away with a folded newspaper. 00:00–00:06 — Static wide view under a simple shelter. The cleaner wipes the last section of the wooden bench, moving moisture toward one end. 00:06–00:12 — Medium side view. The passenger waits until the cleaner lifts the cloth, then points quietly at the seat. The cleaner nods and steps back. 00:12–00:18 — The passenger sits at the dry end. The cleaner folds the same cloth and places it in a bucket. Hold the two people looking toward the water. LOCK: Same jacket, bench slats, bucket, newspaper and seating positions. Dawn light remains cool and steady. AUDIO: Cloth on wood, distant water, gulls well away from camera and a low terminal hum. No dialogue, sentimental music or ferry announcement. AVOID: staged gratitude, extra passengers, a ferry materializing, dry areas becoming wet again, documentary authenticity claims, readable signs or watermark. ``` ## D02 — Along the reed edge **Use:** observational wildlife-style concept **Mode:** text to video · **Format:** 2:1, 20 seconds **Adjust:** weather, not species-specific anatomy. ```text One adult grey heron stands ankle-deep in a shallow reed-fringed pond. Observe from a distant, stationary telephoto viewpoint; this is a synthetic scene, not wildlife footage. 00:00–00:07 — The heron waits with its neck partially folded. Reeds move gently in one breeze; small ripples pass its legs. 00:07–00:14 — It takes one slow deliberate step along the bank, lifting its foot clear before placing it down. The displaced water makes one small ripple. The head stays balanced. 00:14–00:20 — It stops and turns its head slightly toward something outside the frame. Hold the patient posture. No prey capture or takeoff. AUDIO: Reed rustle, distant pond insects and soft water. Do not add a dramatic animal cry. LOCK: One bird, two legs, consistent feather pattern, body scale, water depth and reflection. AVOID: bending beak, extra joints, anthropomorphic expression, bait, approaching camera, attacking prey, repeated identical ripples, music, labels or watermark. ``` ## D03 — The neighborhood repair shelf **Use:** community process explainer **Mode:** text to video · **Format:** 16:9, 20 seconds **Adjust:** object type; keep repair status unambiguous. ```text Illustrate a fictional community repair desk. Three shelf bays carry blank removable cards, with final labels to be added in post. One volunteer in a blue apron handles an unplugged desk fan with a visibly loose front grille. 00:00–00:06 — Wide view: place the fan in the first bay beside its detached grille screw. 00:06–00:13 — Cut to a bench where the volunteer seats the grille and tightens the existing screw with a hand screwdriver. The cable remains unplugged and visible. No electrical testing. 00:13–00:20 — Return the fan to the middle bay, not the final bay. Hold on the blank status card to show it still awaits inspection. AUDIO: Quiet community room, screw contact, shelf tap. English narration exactly: "A repair is one step. Inspection comes before an item returns to use." LOCK: Same fan, screw, cable and volunteer. Use an ordinary modest space. AVOID: spinning blades, live electrical work, invented certification, automatic completion labels, magically restored finish, text, logos or watermark. ``` ## D04 — A letter, not an archive **Use:** clearly fictional period-style reconstruction **Mode:** text to video · **Format:** 4:3, 18 seconds **Adjust:** paper and desk texture, not an unverified historical identity. ```text Create a fictional analog-era domestic scene without claiming a precise place or date. An adult in a plain wool cardigan writes at a wooden desk beside an oil lamp; keep loose fabric away from the flame. 00:00–00:06 — Locked close three-quarter view. The writer finishes one line on paper angled away so no writing is legible. 00:06–00:12 — They fold the sheet in thirds, slide it into a plain envelope and press the flap closed. Show coherent hand contact and paper thickness. 00:12–00:18 — Place the envelope beside a second sealed letter, then look toward a rain-dark window outside focus. End on the pair of envelopes. AUDIO: Pen scratches, paper folds and soft rain. Newly imagined sound, not purported archival audio. No speech or score. LOCK: Same lamp, two envelopes at the end, writing hand, paper and desk grain. AVOID: famous people, invented historical dates, national insignia, fake archive stamps, readable handwriting, film damage obscuring faces, extra letters or watermark. ``` ## D05 — After the rain, at ground level **Use:** small-scale nature observation **Mode:** text to video · **Format:** 16:9, 15 seconds **Adjust:** leaf species after checking its shape. ```text Create one continuous macro observation of a curled fallen leaf on damp forest soil. A single small snail is already partly sheltered beneath it. No other animals. 00:00–00:05 — Camera stays fixed at soil level. One droplet hangs from the lowest leaf tip. The snail's tentacles extend slowly, with no sudden head turn. 00:05–00:10 — The droplet grows from water already on the leaf and falls onto the soil beside, not onto, the snail. Make one subtle splash scaled to the subject. 00:10–00:15 — The snail advances only a few millimeters. Focus remains on its front edge; the shell and wet leaf stay in view. AUDIO: Very quiet distant woodland ambience. No giant footsteps, amplified chewing, dramatic plop or music. LOCK: Leaf veins, shell spiral, animal size, shallow depth of field and diffuse light. AVOID: time-lapse speed, smiling snail, extra eyes, changing shell, upward water, human hands, text or watermark. ``` ## D06 — Measuring the shade **Use:** environmental fieldwork visualization **Mode:** text to video · **Format:** 16:9, 20 seconds **Adjust:** park surface and clothing; measurements must remain fictional. ```text Two adult fieldworkers compare a shaded pavement area with a nearby sunlit area in a generic park. Show a method, never invented measured values. One worker carries a handheld temperature probe with its display facing away. 00:00–00:06 — Locked wide view includes both patches and the same tree. Worker kneels at the sunlit patch, positioning the probe consistently above the surface. 00:06–00:13 — Worker moves along the pavement to the shade boundary and repeats the same posture and probe distance. The second worker observes and writes on an unreadable clipboard. 00:13–00:20 — Medium view of the pair discussing silently; camera settles on the stable light boundary. AUDIO: Footsteps, pen and distant park ambience. No voice-over or electronic reading beep. LOCK: Same equipment, surface, measurement height and sunlight direction. AVOID: fabricated numbers, thermal overlays, guaranteed temperature reduction, changed surfaces, time-of-day jump, unsafe road positioning, text, logos or watermark. ```
description_en: Six observational video briefs — a ferry terminal before dawn, a reed-edge wildlife shot, a community repair shelf, a fictional period reconstruction, ground-level nature after rain and a shade-measurement fieldwork scene.
description_zh: 六条观察式视频简报——黎明前的轮渡码头、芦苇边缘的野生动物镜头、社区维修架、明确虚构的年代场景重建、雨后贴地视角的自然观察，以及测量树荫的野外作业场景。
long_en: These briefs are written against the main risk of documentary-style synthetic footage: passing an illustration off as evidence. The header states that generated scenes are reconstructions, not recordings of real people, places or animal behaviour. The period brief calls itself clearly fictional and forbids attaching an unverified historical identity; the fieldwork brief requires all measurements to remain fictional and bans thermal overlays, readable readings and guaranteed temperature claims; the wildlife brief lets you change weather but not species anatomy. Each has timed beats plus LOCK, AUDIO and AVOID blocks, with staged sentiment, voice-over and sentimental score ruled out.
long_zh: 这组简报针对纪录片风格合成素材的主要风险而写：把示意图当作证据。文件开头即声明生成画面属于场景重建，而非对真实人物、地点或动物行为的记录。年代重建那条自称明确虚构，禁止附会任何未经证实的历史人物身份；野外作业那条要求所有测量数值保持虚构，禁止热成像叠加、可读读数与降温效果承诺；野生动物那条允许更换天气，但不得改动物种解剖结构。每条都带节拍时间线与 LOCK、AUDIO、AVOID 段落，并排除刻意煽情、旁白与煽情配乐。
sec_note_en: Plain text prompts; no tool access or external calls. Output is synthetic and must be labelled as a reconstruction or illustration — never presented as documentary evidence, and the briefs say so themselves. Written and named for FLUX 3, whose availability is staged; the directing structure transfers to other video models but exact behaviour will not. A same-named file exists in a second repo under the flaqai account with different scenes; both are run by the commercial API reseller bestimage.ai / flaq.ai, though these prompt files carry no product placement.
sec_note_zh: 纯文本提示词，不涉及工具调用或外部请求。生成结果属于合成素材，必须标注为场景重建或示意画面——不得当作纪实证据呈现，简报本身也是这么写的。以 FLUX 3 命名与撰写，而该模型分阶段开放；这套导演式结构可迁移到其它视频模型，但具体表现不会一致。flaqai 账号下的另一同名仓库存在同名文件但场景不同；两者均由商业 API 转售商 bestimage.ai / flaq.ai 运营，不过这些提示词文件没有产品植入。
